parameters.content:
## HMAC is computed over the RAW body

The webhook runs with **Raw Body ON**, so the payload arrives as binary and the Crypto node hashes those exact bytes.

**Never hash re-serialised JSON.** Parsing and re-stringifying changes key order, spacing and unicode escaping, so the digest stops matching and every legitimate Shopify delivery gets rejected. That is the classic Shopify HMAC bug.

Secret lives in the `crypto` credential (hmacSecret) — not in the code, not in an env var.

## Shopify re-fires on EVERY cart edit

So the write goes through `case2_upsert_cart()` — one atomic statement keyed on checkout_token.

It updates cart CONTENTS and deliberately never touches `next_touch_at`, `touches_sent`, `status` or `opted_out`. Otherwise a customer fiddling with their cart would slide the schedule forward forever and never get a message — and an opted-out customer could be resurrected.

Proven by 10 DB-level checks, see testing-log 2026-08-02.

parameters.content:
## Gender is inferred ONCE, here — not per touch

Workflow 02 relaxes its Arabic feminine-form rules for a customer we know to be **female** (arabic-master-reference.md §5, ruled 2026-08-07). That safety depends on this signal being right.

**Why intake and not the sender:** gender is a property of the customer, so it must not change between touch 1 and touch 3. `case2_upsert_cart` makes it sticky on exactly the same terms as locale — correctable while `touches_sent = 0`, frozen after.

**`unknown` is a correct answer.** It asks the model for gender-neutral phrasing and keeps the checker strict. A wrong guess is visible to a native speaker on a real handset; neutral phrasing never is.

**The trap:** the ة / اء / ى endings say "feminine", but أسامة، حمزة، مصطفى، يحيى، ضياء are all male. Explicit name lists are therefore checked BEFORE the morphology rules. Latin script has no ending rule at all — a trailing "a" would misgender Mustafa and Zakaria.

Haiku is asked only for **Arabic** carts with an unrecognised name: agreement is meaningless in en/fr and a paid call that changes nothing is a real client bill.
